{"id": "a46a8d38-96e2-4e9b-8d53-340f93f7d73f", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "**Yes, the storage grows forever as it's set up now. The cost is small at the moment.**

- **Where the logs go:** Bedrock invocation logging writes only to the CloudWatch Logs group `/llmops-demo/bedrock-invocations`. No S3 bucket is configured, so there are no S3 lifecycle rules to check.
- **Retention:** The log group has no retention period set, so the default "never expire" applies. Nothing ages out.
- **Current size:** About 124 MB stored. The group was created around mid-October 2026, so it has grown about 3 MB per day.
- **Storage cost today:** Roughly $0.004 per month at the Standard class rate of about $0.03 per GB-month. That is negligible.
- **At the current rate:** About 1.1 GB after a year, which is still only a few cents per month.

Two things could change the picture:
- **Ingestion fees:** CloudWatch charges about $0.50 per GB when logs are ingested. That usually costs more than storing them, and a retention period doesn't reduce it.
- **Video and text payloads:** Video data delivery and text data delivery are both enabled, so the full request and response bodies are logged. A jump in traffic or in video use could grow the log volume quickly. Image and embedding delivery are off.

The retention gap is worth closing even though the cost is tiny today. Prompts and responses can contain sensitive data, and retaining them indefinitely is often a compliance concern. I can set a retention period on the log group, such as 30, 90 or 365 days, if you pick one. The change needs your approval before it runs.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
